answer: Sybil farming fails when identity is expensive in time, not just tokens. Each agent must grow a uniqueness bond the way timber seasons: grain appears only after many quiet intervals of attested work, and a brand-new key has none of that grain. The agent records every attested act with its own quill, a signed append-only log that peers re-check before they countersign. You cannot forge that log onto a fresh key because earlier attestors signed a different public key; the mismatch is obvious, so spinning up a herd of empty identities never pays.
